title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The crossed-out initial formulas pair the functors wrongly. One reads L_i Λ^j(M,n) ≃ L_{i+n} Γ^j(M,n+1), whereas the correct statement is LΛ^i(X[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(X)[i]. Grothendieck crossed them out himself.

The first written long sequence pairs Sym with Λ: 0 → Sym^i K → Sym^{i-1}K ⊗ Λ^1E → … → Λ^iE → Λ^i K(M,n+1) → 0. This is the de Rham-type Koszul complex, which is exact only in characteristic 0 (or with denominators). The integrally exact version uses Γ in place of Sym, and the page indeed rewrites it with Γ^i K(M,n) just below.
Shift signs in the final lines ([-i], [-2i] together with L_{*-i}) follow a nonstandard or ambiguous convention. The boxed L_r Sym^i K(M,n+1) ≃ L_{r-i} Λ^i K(M,n) is the correct form.

ideas.what: Décalage isomorphisms L Sym^i(X[1]) ≃ LΛ^i(X)[i], LΛ^i(X[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(X)[i], L Sym^i(X[2]) ≃ LΓ^i(X)[2i]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen, Bousfield; written up by Illusie (Complexe cotangent I, 1971)

ideas.what: Proof via the Koszul complexes attached to the simplicial path fibration K(M,n) → E(M,n+1) → K(M,n+1)
ideas.modern_name: Koszul complexes for a short exact sequence of flat modules; simplicial path space

ideas.what: Use of décalage to compute weight-graded homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces (with the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe derived functors and the homology of K(M,n)

deep.surprise_reason: These are lecture-prep notes reproducing the known Quillen–Bousfield–Illusie décalage, and the page itself cites Illusie. Nothing new; the only mild interest is that it documents Grothendieck connecting décalage and the homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces to the divided-power de Rham theme in 1976.
transcription_corrections: The line '0 → Γ^i K(M,n) → Γ^{i-1}K(M,n) ⊗ Λ^1 E(…)' is separate. The right-hand '… → Sym^i E(M,n+1) → Sym^i K(M,n+1) → 0' belongs to the Λ^i K(M,n) sequence on the line above, not to the Γ line.
The first long sequence ends '→ Λ^i E(M,n+1) → Λ^i K(M,n+1) → 0'.
The crossed-out formulas read 'L_i Sym^i(M,n) ≃ L_{i+n} Λ^j(M,n+1)' and 'L_i Λ^j(M,n) ≃ L_{i+n} Γ^j(M,n+1)'. The indices are partly illegible, and the second formula is not fully struck through.
The second display line is 'L_* F(M,n)' and 'L_* F(M[n])'.
The 'M → M' at the right is probably 'M ⊂ M' or an identity sketch, and is unclear.
